ops.title: Bonjour goodbye packets require graceful shutdown
ops.body:
The `_cc-runtime._tcp` mDNS advertisement is only withdrawn when the daemon shuts down gracefully. `access.BonjourHook` (access/bonjour.go) registers the zeroconf server and, on `<-ctx.Done()`, calls `server.Shutdown()` to emit mDNS goodbye packets (TTL=0) that flush the record from browser/mDNSResponder caches.

For that to run before the process exits, the daemon must WAIT for the hook. cc-interact's `daemon.startHTTP` now runs the `OnHTTPStart` hook on the wait group (`s.wg`), mirroring `Background`, so `Serve` blocks on `s.wg.Wait()` until the hook returns after the serve context is cancelled (fixed 2026-07-14, cc-interact commit a03428b). Before that fix the hook was fire-and-forget and the goodbye raced — and lost — the process exit, leaving a stale advertisement.

The normal restart path is graceful: `pair` / `pair --off` restart the daemon via a Shutdown RPC that cancels the serve context, so goodbye packets flush. The one gap: a SIGKILLed daemon (e.g. eviction that times out and force-kills a wedged holder) skips `Shutdown()` entirely, so the record lingers until browsers age it out on TTL (~a couple minutes). Inherent to mDNS, not a bug to fix.

Verified on-host 2026-07-14: a pty-backed `dns-sd -B _cc-runtime._tcp local.` showed 5 `Add` records for instance `yasyf-home` while paired, then 5 explicit `Rmv` records within ~11s of `pair --off`; a fresh browse afterward showed nothing.</body>
